answer: Agents could earn spendable credits by completing randomly assigned, tamper-evident tasks whose results are checked against independent agents and occasional human audits. Credits unlock higher-value tasks only after a history of accepted work, while disputed results are slashed. A sybil can create many identities cheaply, but each must produce verifiable work and build its own track record; splitting identities does not multiply earned credit. Even if shale, timber, and ridge are task labels, the attacker still pays in compute, time, and forfeited rewards for each identity.
